### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. Malan overgrowth syndrome  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.783)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:7788)

**Proposed mechanism:** NFIX (HGNC:7788) —DISRUPTS→ Regulation of neurogenesis and gliogenesis (GO:0007410); Regulation of neurogenesis and gliogenesis (GO:0007410) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal cerebral white matter morphology (HP:0033713); NFIX (HGNC:7788) —DISRUPTS→ Regulation of neurogenesis and gliogenesis (GO:0007410); Regulation of neurogenesis and gliogenesis (GO:0007410) —LEADS_TO→ Overgrowth syndrome (HP:0011351). Haploinsufficiency of NFIX disrupts the regulation of neurogenesis and gliogenesis, leading to abnormal cerebral white matter morphology in MONDO:0011244 and contributing to overgrowth syndrome phenotypes in Malan overgrowth syndrome (MONDO:0013885).

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in NFIX with a demonstrable gain-of-function mechanism in either disease, or the absence of NFIX variants in individuals with these phenotypes. _(variant: rs145714823)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of NFIX haploinsufficiency in these distinct neurodevelopmental and overgrowth conditions could lead to targeted therapeutic strategies for modulating NFIX function or downstream pathways to alleviate shared or distinct phenotypic features.

#### 2. brain malformations with or without urinary tract defects  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.477)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-73980, Reactome:R-HSA-749476)

**Proposed mechanism:** NFIX (HGNC:7786) —DISRUPTS→ neuronal development and gliogenesis (GO:0048698); NFIA (HGNC:7784) —DISRUPTS→ neuronal development and gliogenesis (GO:0048698); neuronal development and gliogenesis (GO:0048698) —LEADS_TO→ Cerebellar hypoplasia (HP:0001341); neuronal development and gliogenesis (GO:0048698) —LEADS_TO→ Pontine hypoplasia (HP:0031645); neuronal development and gliogenesis (GO:0048698) —LEADS_TO→ Brain malformations (HP:0002072); neuronal development and gliogenesis (GO:0048698) —LEADS_TO→ Urinary tract defects (HP:0000077). Loss-of-function variants in NFIX and NFIA disrupt the critical pathway of neuronal development and gliogenesis, leading to the overlapping phenotypes of cerebellar hypoplasia, pontine hypoplasia, and general brain malformations, with a subset of patients also exhibiting urinary tract defects.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in NFIX or NFIA that lead to a gain-of-function mechanism in either disease, or demonstration that the disease modules for MONDO:0011244 and MONDO:0100478 are entirely independent and do not converge on shared developmental pathways. _(variant: A pathogenic variant in NFIX or NFIA with a population frequency > 0.01 in gnomAD.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of NFIX and NFIA in these distinct but mechanistically linked developmental disorders could lead to the identification of common therapeutic targets or biomarkers for brain malformations and related congenital anomalies. It highlights the importance of studying transcription factor networks in neurodevelopmental disorders.

#### 3. macrocephaly, acquired, with impaired intellectual development  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.476)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-73980, Reactome:R-HSA-749476)

**Proposed mechanism:** NFIX (HGNC:7756) —DISRUPTS→ Regulation of neuronal development and migration (GO:0021987); NFIB (HGNC:7757) —DISRUPTS→ Regulation of neuronal development and migration (GO:0021987); Regulation of neuronal development and migration (GO:0021987) —LEADS_TO→ Intellectual disability (HP:0001249); Regulation of neuronal development and migration (GO:0021987) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal cerebral sulcation (HP:0030718); Regulation of neuronal development and migration (GO:0021987) —LEADS_TO→ Macrocephaly (HP:0000256). Disruption of NFIX and NFIB function, which are crucial for normal neuronal development and migration, leads to intellectual disability, abnormal cerebral sulcation, and macrocephaly, linking MONDO:0011244 and MONDO:0032658 through a shared developmental pathway.

**How to falsify it:** Absence of pathogenic variants in NFIX or NFIB in individuals diagnosed with MONDO:0011244 or MONDO:0032658, or demonstration that the shared phenotypes arise from entirely distinct molecular pathways not involving NFIX/NFIB regulation. _(variant: Presence of common benign variants in NFIX/NFIB in gnomAD that do not segregate with either disease.)_

#### 4. Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease, demyelinating, IIA 1I  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.469)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-73980, Reactome:R-HSA-749476)

**Proposed mechanism:** POLR3B (HGNC:9339) —DISRUPTS→ RNA polymerase III transcription (GO:0006357); RNA polymerase III transcription (GO:0006357) —DECREASES→ neuronal development (GO:0048666); neuronal development (GO:0048666) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal cerebral white matter morphology (HP:0005386); neuronal development (GO:0048666) —LEADS_TO→ Cerebellar hypoplasia (HP:0001347); RNA polymerase III transcription (GO:0006357) —DECREASES→ myelination (GO:0007287); myelination (GO:0007287) —LEADS_TO→ Peripheral demyelination (HP:0003494); myelination (GO:0007287) —LEADS_TO→ Distal muscle weakness (HP:0002460). Loss-of-function mutations in POLR3B disrupt RNA polymerase III transcription, which in turn impairs downstream pathways critical for neuronal development and myelination. This disruption leads to the distinct phenotypes observed in both MONDO:0011244 (e.g., abnormal white matter, cerebellar hypoplasia) and Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease, demyelinating, IIA 1I (e.g., peripheral demyelination, distal muscle weakness).
